name: plan-from-interview
description: Turn source material into an approved, traceable plan, publish milestones and tickets, and record a planning retrospective. Stop at the tickets; never start a build.

steps.name: intake
steps.description: Choose a slug and copy the whiteboard photo, interview transcript and braindump, when supplied, to planning/<slug>/raw/. Preserve originals and number text lines. If no transcript exists, run a structured interview one question at a time and save each question and answer word for word. Cover the outcome and its date, users, in and out of scope, known work, dependencies, risks, who decides, capacity and how done is proved. Record the tracker (GitHub or Linear), target repository or project, and available tool names. Do not publish anything.

steps.name: extract
steps.description:
First record the board's legend in planning/<slug>/plan.json with source locators: units or estimate scale, owner letters, priority tags, arrows and colours. Keep unknown meanings unclear. Then transcribe the whiteboard to planning/<slug>/raw/whiteboard.txt before interpreting items. Give every box, column, arrow and table a stable locator. Preserve original text and keep translations separately. Write each claim with id, text, source and status read, inferred or open. A model's reading is read, never confirmed.

For each item, preserve its circled estimate and units, priority tag, owner letters, horizon and column when present. Store each field with value, source and status: read, inferred or unclear. Read each field through the legend; an unclear priority does not make the whole item unclear. Raise unclear fields as open questions. Record each arrow as a claim with kind: "relationship", from and to item claim ids, source locators, direction and legend-based meaning. Record duplicates across sources as claims with kind: "duplicate", from and to claim ids. Preserve both source records. Ask about uncertain endpoints or meanings; do not assume an arrow means dependency.

Preserve capacity tables with labels, units and time periods, values, source locators and claim ids. When the board shows a total, add its parts using matching units and time periods; record the shown total, sum and difference. Raise each mismatch as an open question. Record each existing issue as owner/repo#N; use read-only tracker lookup to record its state and URL. Raise a closed issue or failed lookup as an open question. Extract acceptance criteria only from a person or a cited source. Keep all field and capacity evidence attached to its claims. Follow docs/planning.md.

steps.name: reconcile
steps.exit_condition: weft check-plan planning/<slug>/plan.json exits 0 and no open questions remain.
steps.description:
List all open questions: disagreements, unclear fields or legend meanings, relationship and duplicate claims, total mismatches, closed issues and missing acceptance criteria. Ask a named person one question at a time. Only a named person may confirm a claim; record who confirmed it with their verbatim answer and source locator. Keep the original evidence.

Run weft check-plan planning/<slug>/plan.json without --allow-open. Fix errors and use step loop-continue while questions remain. Do not drop or downgrade questions to pass the check. Use step loop-done only when the checker exits 0 and no open questions remain. If no person can answer, stop at reconcile and report all open questions. Do not draft final tickets. At the iteration limit, stop for human resolution; never treat the limit as approval.

steps.name: draft
steps.exit_condition: weft check-plan planning/<slug>/plan.json exits zero and plan.md matches plan.json.
steps.description:
Write milestones and tickets to planning/<slug>/plan.json and plan.md using docs/planning.md. Every ticket has why, in_spec, out_of_spec, done_when, dependencies and claim_ids. Carry through field values and statuses, estimates, priorities, owners, horizons, original text and capacity evidence. Map resolved dependency relationship claims to ticket dependencies; preserve other relationships and duplicate evidence. Reuse verified existing_issue links instead of creating duplicate issues.

Acceptance criteria must come from a person or a cited source; cite that evidence for each done_when entry. Never invent acceptance criteria to fill a field. Missing criteria are open questions: stop and return to reconcile. Account for every confirmed claim by citation or a dropped entry with a reason. Cite claims for milestone dates. Run weft check-plan planning/<slug>/plan.json without --allow-open; fix errors and regenerate plan.md. Use step loop-continue for another draft and step loop-done only when the checker exits 0 and plan.md matches plan.json. Stop for human help at the iteration limit.

steps.name: review
steps.exit_condition: A person has read plan.md and explicitly approved this exact plan revision; approval is recorded.
steps.description: Have a person read planning/<slug>/plan.md, including dropped claims, capacity, existing issue links and inferred assumptions. Record their approval and the plan revision it covers. Requested changes use step loop-continue to return to draft, then require a fresh review. Use step loop-done only with explicit approval. Stop for human resolution at the iteration limit.

steps.name: publish

guards.message: GitHub issues may be created only during publish after plan approval
GitHub project items may be added only during publish after plan approval
GitHub milestone API writes may run only during publish after plan approval
Linear MCP writes may run only during publish after plan approval

steps.description:
This is the only step that may create milestones or tickets or write to the tracker. Re-run the checker and confirm approval still covers the current plan. Before any ticket write, check its approved done_when criteria. If a ticket has no approved criteria, do not publish it; return to reconcile and report the missing criteria.

Write the approved done_when criteria under ## Gates, one line per criterion in plan order: - G1: <approved criterion>, - G2: <approved criterion>, and so on. Never invent gates. Preserve approved test or check annotations; do not invent test paths or checks. When out_of_spec names excluded paths, write ## Out of scope and copy each path verbatim on its own bullet line. Omit that section when no excluded paths are named.

Publish to the recorded GitHub or Linear target using only the guarded write commands or tools. First read planning/<slug>/published.json and look up existing_issue links; reuse those issues instead of creating them. Use stable plan ids plus a plan-specific marker in tracker items, and read the tracker for that marker before every create or retry, including after an uncertain response. Reuse matching milestones and project memberships too. After each created, linked or recovered item, atomically update published.json with the plan id, tracker id, URL and revision. If interrupted between a tracker write and the journal update, recover by marker lookup before retrying; never blindly create again. Publish only the approved content and stop at tickets; do not implement them or start a build.

steps.name: verify
steps.exit_condition: The tracker readback matches plan.json and published.json, with every milestone and ticket accounted for and no duplicates.
steps.description: Read milestones, tickets, existing issue links, project membership and dependencies back from the tracker and compare with planning/<slug>/plan.json and published.json. Save the comparison. Use step loop-continue to return to publish for approved-content repairs at most twice; when the limit is reached, stop and report unresolved mismatches. Plan changes require renewed human review. Use step loop-done only when the readback matches, then continue to retrospective. Never start a build.

steps.name: retrospective
steps.description:
Write planning/<slug>/retro.md using this fixed format. In a shared repo use roles, not people; keep examples generic. Use the run's actual start date and leave finished empty until the build-out section is written.

---
plan: <slug>
project: <repo or project name>
started: YYYY-MM-DD
finished:
---

## Planning

### Went well
- What worked. Evidence: a link, a test name, a count or a source line from this run.

### Fell short
- [drag] What cost time or quality. Evidence: ...
- [defect] <project>/<slug>: What broke. Evidence: ...

### Change next time
- One concrete change to the workflow, with evidence from this run.

Every item must cite Evidence: from this run. Read the saved checker output, the review, the answers to open questions and publication results; a ticket publish failure is evidence even if a retry succeeded. A [drag] is a process cost; a [defect] is a bug and names the project and slug. Do not invent evidence, test names, links, counts or answers; omit any item with no evidence. A subsection with nothing to report says - None. Replace the example bullets with supported findings. Base each concrete change on cited evidence. Preserve existing frontmatter and sections on a retry; do not duplicate ## Planning. Do not add ## Build-out yet or start implementation. If writing the retrospective fails, report that failure and continue without changing the plan's result.
